variant_decisions.evidence: Qere חַטֹּאתָיו is plural (Ncfpc/Sp3ms); ketiv חטאתו is singular (Ncfsc/Sp3ms); same lemma (2403 b) and suffix. The ASV opens the verse "for his sins which he sinned" — plural — and renders the unvaried singular of the same noun later in the same verse as "and in his sin which he did", so the number is visible in the English. The plural distinguishes the qere.

variant_decisions.evidence: Qere וּבִשְׂגוּב and ketiv ובשגיב are the same proper name (lemma c/b/7687), tagged C/R/Np in both, differing only in the vowel letter: waw in the qere, yod in the ketiv. Unlike a purely defective spelling, the difference survives transliteration — the ASV's "his youngest son Segub" carries the qere's u, where the ketiv consonants would give Segib. The name distinguishes the qere.
